title: How efficient are our minisplit heat pumps in the winter
summary: A New Brunswick homeowner instruments two mini-splits through winter and finds they use about half the electricity of resistance heat, with defrost in humid weather the main penalty.

assertions.quote: I think those mini splits heat with about half as much electricity as conventional electric heaters would.
whenever it defrosts, that basically means heating up the outside coils using electricity, and that is electricity that isn't used to heat up the house
there doesn't seem to be any correlation of coefficient of performance and outside temperature
with electricity being relatively cheap here and natural gas expensive, that makes it the most cost-effective heating option here
they're also an air conditioning system, and an air conditioning system that pays for itself
the mini splits don't put the heat exactly where we want it when we want it.
